purpose: Replace the twelve-hour inactivity limit the owner rejected with one hour, and fifteen minutes for the roles this platform already calls privileged. The first version of this control chose twelve hours on the argument that field users are interrupted by the job, so a shorter limit would be worked around; that argument treated the session as the only way to preserve work in progress and set the limit by the UX budget rather than by risk.
requiredInvariants: One authority for who is privileged. The tier is decided from the role on the session context row this same function is validating - not from staffRoles, not from a second lookup - and the set is ROLES_REQUIRING_MFA, the platform's existing definition. A second notion of privileged here would be the inconsistency V6.3.4 is about.
A malformed, unknown or absent role falls to the ordinary one-hour limit, never to no limit. A case asserts this for empty string, an unknown value, null and undefined.

The product pathway is not given a faked tier. A product session carries a scope and not a platform role, so there is no role on that row to decide from, and reaching for staffRoles to invent one would create the second authority this pass refused. It keeps the ordinary limit, from the same shared constant.

Step-up controls are not relaxed to compensate. The financial MFA freshness requirement and the control-plane step-up are untouched; the idle limit bounds ambient exposure and does not stand in front of the risky operations alone.
The absolute thirty-day lifetime is a separate limit and stays separate, as instructed.

The rejected reasoning is left visible in SESSION_POLICY.md rather than deleted. A policy document that quietly replaces its own justification is the class of untrue record this programme keeps finding.
No schema change, no migration, no new dependency. 1C, marketing and presentation are not touched, and no production, REG.RU, DNS or credential mutation is performed.
acceptance: session-idle-timeout.spec.ts passes 12 of 12 and the whole auth module passes 634.
Three mutations are caught: removing the privileged tier fails 1 of 12, letting an absent role become unbounded fails 1, and making the check site stop consulting the role fails 1.
The prior test asserted a four-hour FLOOR on the limit - an assertion encoding the rejected reasoning - and is replaced rather than loosened, because it was protecting the wrong property.

V7.1.1 and V7.3.1 were both rejected by the matrix when the number changed, which is the self-revoking mechanism working, and are rebound to the limits actually in force. The matrix returns to applied 332 / rejected 0 with no verdict moved.
